records.text: Lance Wallnau graduated from a military academy and his father Carl Wallnau was a major in the United States Air Force who served under General Patton
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: His father, Carl Wallnau, was a major in the United States Air Force
He graduated from a military academy. His father, Carl Wallnau, was a major in the United States Air Force. Wallnau served under General Patton.

verification.notes: Wikipedia confirms that Lance Wallnau attended Valley Forge Military Academy and College (supporting the graduation from a military academy) and that his father, Carl Wallnau, was an Air Force major. However, no reliable sources, including Wikipedia or other web results, mention Carl Wallnau serving under General Patton. This part of the claim appears unverifiable based on available information; verification would require access to military service records (e.g., via FOIA request to the National Archives or Department of Defense personnel files) to confirm any WWII-era service details under Patton's command.

records.text: BILT received nearly $8 million in June 2025 from the Department of Defense, including $7.4 million from the Air Force and just under a quarter-million dollars from the Navy.

records.text: On September 9, a U.S. Air Force plane left Fort Huachuca at 11:43 a.m. local time and flew to El Paso, Texas.

verification.notes: The surviving AirNav record confirms SAM702 and tail 99-0404 in southern Arizona on September 9, 2025, first seen near Tucson and landing at Eloy. It does not establish an 11:43 Fort Huachuca departure or a flight to El Paso.

records.text: The plane landed in El Paso at 1:31 p.m. local time after a 50-minute hop from Fort Huachuca.

verification.notes: AirNav independently confirms that USAF tail 99-0404 operated as SAM702 in southern Arizona on September 9, 2025. The available record does not establish the claimed El Paso-to-Andrews leg.
